findings.reason: the stated cause selects the freeze branch over the drop branch, so a node reading only the section is steered at the wrong repair for a misdescription it has no way to check.
findings.text: §30's Why states the budget view composes "figures that move with the clock, and the two surfaces' calls are seconds apart under load", but under this test's own isolated fixture the composition carries no clock-derived figure at all: advancing the clock 30 s between the two calls changes exactly one leaf path, `.checked_at` (`evidence/captured.json`), while `age_seconds`, `seconds_until_reset`, `resume_after_seconds` and `mean_age_seconds` are unmoved; the Deliverable's remedy for that class — "the parity case freezes the clock the view reads for both calls" — is therefore the wrong branch here, and it invites a repair reaching past the declared write path into the clock production composes from, where a one-line change to the dropped set is what the section's own rule calls for

findings.reason: a node landing the stamp branch cannot satisfy the declared control as written, and must either improvise a control that also un-drops the key or take the freeze branch to keep the control honest, so the done-when as stated does not measure the repair it names.
findings.text: §30's Done-when requires "a negative control that advances the clock by 30 seconds between the two calls fails it", but that control cannot fire under the repair the section's own rule prescribes: with `checked_at` dropped from the comparison (the stamp branch, exactly as `composed_at` is already dropped) the parity case passes while the probe still advances the clock 30 s per composition (`evidence/run-drop.log`, `EXIT=0`, `1 passed in 7.85s`; `evidence/captured-drop.json` shows the clock still stepping a minute per pair), because the sole clock-derived field is the one the branch drops
